newsitem.title: UK: Royal Dutch/Shell sticks to Shell Canada.
newsitem.headline: Royal Dutch/Shell sticks to Shell Canada.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group said it will stick to its 78 percent stake in Shell Canada, which earlier announced the sale of its chemical business to a unit of its Anglo-Dutch majority stakeholder.
"The stake remains unchanged: 78 percent owned by Royal Dutch/Shell Group and 22 percent owned by the minority public shareholders," a Royal Dutch/Shell Group spokesman said.
"It is purely the chemicals business this deal applies to," the spokesman said.
His comments come after Shell Canada's vice-president Ron Blakely said he knew of no Royal Dutch/Shell Group intention to sell any of its interest.

Shell Canada's chemicals business was sold to Shell International so that the operations would be better positioned to fight competition in an increasingly global market, the Royal Dutch/Shell spokesman said.
He added that the deal would not change the chemical production or the marketing set-up in Canada.
"If anything, staffing levels will go up in that chemicals business," he said.
